newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet, no trade - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet, no trade - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were slow amid light packer inquiry and no reported trades, feedlot sources said.
There were a few bids at $65.00 to $66.00 per cwt that were passed by owners asking $68.00 to $69.00, they said.

Cattle continued to recover from the unusual late April snowstorm on Friday that dumped heavy rain and up to 13 inches of wet snow mostly in the Hereford and Amarillo areas. Some death loss was reported among light-weight calves that had just been shipped from Mexico or southern Texas and were not able to withstand the rain, snow and cold, the sources said.

Actual numbers were not available, as feedlot operators continued to evaluate the storm's impact, but there was talk that some feedlots lost 60 to 80 calves weighing 200 to 500 lbs. Cattle on feedlots less than a week were affected the most, they said.
"Some of them calves were Mexican short-hairs that weren't acclimated, or were weak anyway," a feedyard manager in Hereford said.
Market-ready cattle at the affected feedlots fought muddy pen conditions and were thrown off feed during the storm, but were recovering quickly, they said.
